precepts.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup. Read at the breaking of bread, and it is the same instruction we opened with in Lamentations 3: let us search and try our ways.
precepts.point: For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Zechariah ends with the Lord saving “the flock of his people”, lifted up “as the stones of a crown”, filled like the bowls and the corners of the altar, drinking and making “a noise as through wine”. At the breaking of bread the class read Paul's instruction for those who drink of the Lord's cup now: “But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.”

It is the same instruction the class opened with in Lamentations: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Before a man eats of that bread and drinks of that cup, he has to search himself and try his ways.

So the cup of the Lord now is a call to examine ourselves and turn again to the Lord. The wine and the rejoicing of Zechariah belong to the flock he saves in that day: the twelve tribes that searched and tried their ways and turned back to him, the stones of his crown lifted up upon his land.

precepts.text: Was Christ ever confused about his position and role with the Father? I can of mine own self do nothing: I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me. Christ understands his role and position, and Christ tells us the husband is the head of the wife. So why is there still so much confusion? Somebody does not believe like they say they do.
precepts.point: If you are scared of your wife, you cannot get out here and cast down the lies of the nations and bring us out of this captivity when you are scared to deal with your own house.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Is anybody confused on the order? Then why are there so many problems in Israel, so much confusion about the husband's position and the wife's position? Because pride has made its way in, and confusion has set itself in the house.

“and the head of Christ is God”. Was Christ ever confused, at any moment in his life, about his position and role with the Father? He said: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

Christ said, I am doing exactly as the Father told me to do. Is he doing what he wants? No. Christ understands his role and his position. And Christ now tells us the husband is the head of the wife. So why is there still so much confusion? Somebody does not believe like they say they do.

It happens on both sides of the room. Brother, because of your lack of leadership, because you are non-confrontational and passive and don't want no smoke, she raises her voice and you cower; she walks by shoulder-bumping you, and you can't raise your voice in your own house. All because you gave up your position. Some brothers want to be mama's boys: you didn't want a wife, you wanted a mom. If Christ submits to the head over him, the husband must take his place under Christ, and the wife her place under her husband.

precepts.text: We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously: the broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice, that he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but are you eating the bread that is abundant for us? The breaking of bread is also symbolic of that manna and the commitment we have to consume God's word every day.
precepts.point: He took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously. Paul received it of the Lord: “the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.” Then “This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.”

The broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice: he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but are you eating the bread that is abundant for us? Breaking bread once a week and thinking that is all right is not enough. The breaking of bread is also symbolic of that manna and the commitment we have to consume God's word every day, day and night.

Revelation 2:17 promises it: “To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna”. The body is dying; you are born and on a path to death. The flesh fights, the mind forgets, and the soul is weighed down by this tabernacle, so the inward man has to be renewed and kept alive by the word daily. The manna showed it, the prophets lived it, David meditated on it, Paul explained it, and Christ revealed himself to be that true bread from heaven. “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.”

In the wilderness Israel sacrificed daily, twice daily. Psalm 51: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it”, but “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” If we really considered our ways, our thoughts and our behaviors, we would understand why we need to seek him daily and continually to forgive our sins; feeding yourself so sparingly, you won't understand this.

precepts.text: If a woman will not be covered let her be shorn, and since that is a shame, let her be covered; a man with long hair is a shame to him, and a woman's long hair is her glory and her covering.
precepts.point: We laugh about old sins to keep you from being too hard on yourself. A brother who battled the same-sex lifestyle is told to cut his hair low, and a shapely sister who was promiscuous to wear a bigger dress and talk to no one for years, with the ladies in waiting programme to keep her busy; idle time is the danger. That is advice, not a law, and a step towards fixing it.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Christ says the Galileans Pilate killed and the eighteen crushed by the tower were not sinners above all others: “except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.” Sin is sin, and there is repentance for it regardless. Part of that repentance is setting things up in your life so you can get better, and Paul dealt with the same issue in Corinth. Corinth was Greece, and the Greeks were heavily into that lifestyle.

“For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn”: if she won't cover her head, shave all her hair off. “but if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered”. It is a shame, so put a hair wrap on. “For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God: but the woman is the glory of the man.”

“Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him? But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.” Samson had locks, so how is long hair a shame? The shame was how they wore it and styled it in Greece, which led to what is read in 1 Corinthians 6.

So a brother who battles or has battled the same-sex lifestyle is told to cut his hair, not to shame or embarrass him, but as a remedy: you can't do that with a fade. And a sister who was heavily promiscuous and very shapely is told she's got a big ass, wear a bigger dress, cover yourself up, in here and outside, to take the attention off you. Then don't talk to nobody for four, five years till you get yourself together; that's why there is the ladies in waiting program, to teach discipline and keep you busy, because idle time is the danger. This is advice, not a law, a step towards fixing it. Pride goeth before the fall.

precepts.text: For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man. Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. So many people spend their whole lives fighting against their God given purpose, and you wonder why you have all these spirits of depression and anxiety: it is because you are fighting against your God given role. You cannot change it, and when you try to change it, it only brings confusion. The sooner you accept the truth of the matter, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself. Sometimes the help starts to think that she is the purpose; no, you are the help meet for me and my house.
precepts.point: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Just as he had dominion over the other creatures, he had dominion over the woman: he named her. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Just as Adam had dominion over the creatures he named, he named her. So there is no confusion about why the woman was made, Paul says: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” “Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.”

People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? They do not know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. God created the woman for the man, and nobody can create or remake their own purpose in life.

So many people, men and women, spend their lives fighting against their God-given purpose. It is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not. And you wonder why you are dealing with spirits of depression and anxiety and always on edge: it is because you are fighting against your God-given role. You cannot change it, and trying only brings confusion.

Out of all the beasts of the field there was nothing fit for the man, so God made him a woman, and that woman has a purpose: help meet for her husband. Sometimes the help starts to think she is the purpose, that she is the house. No: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself; turmoil comes when you leave that place.

That is where it all went left. Eve knew the rule, but the serpent spoke to what was already within her: “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She wanted the position that was over her. Paul goes back to the beginning for the same reason: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” And Sirach says, “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” All she had to do was stay in her role and in order.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. But the first woman, the first created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife ain't? That is why the head has to keep reminding them of their place and role in the home.

precepts.text: For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church. Is there any confusion there?
precepts.point: The head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. Paul is not making anything up or creating a list; he went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Paul is not making anything up. He is not creating a list and saying, I'll place this person here and that person there. He went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning, when Adam named his wife Eve, and he does it in other places too.

Ephesians says it again: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Is there any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church.

So the order runs: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or out of their position, what are they? The damn devil. That goes for the men too: men who step out of their role and want to be a mama's boy, you are the damn devil. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

There cannot be a commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle with something, and we know the fight, but never be the one who says, I can get with everything else but that right there I just can't do; he's an idiot, I can't follow him. That is not what the scripture said.

precepts.text: And he is the head of the body, the church. Christ is the head of the church.
precepts.point: The head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God. Paul is not making anything up or creating a list; he went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“the head of every man is Christ”. Colossians shows it: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead”. Christ is the head of the church.

And Christ himself is under a head: “the head of Christ is God.” Christ said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do”. And, “the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth”. How could the Father show the Son if the Son was the Father? If you are still stuck on the Trinity, go sit in the corner. It makes no sense for the Most High to show his Son something if they are the same entity.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given, and the headship of the household falls under the same order. “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” To honour the Son is to honour what he said; if you do not honour the order God has given you, you are not honouring the Lord.

Christ said, “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He is letting us know that he himself is in the divine order and submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did?

precepts.text: Keep the ordinances as I delivered them to you: the head of every man is Christ, the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. Grounded in that order, love becomes stronger, joy and passion follow, and the marriage becomes more durable over time.
precepts.point: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord: the same way you submit to Christ and the Most High, not less and not below it. Scripture defines marriage by function, not feelings. Traditions carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. Function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Paul praises the brethren that they “keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.” Then he gives the summary of the order: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.”

This is the same order as Ephesians 5:23: “the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” The woman’s list of duties may look longer, but the man’s responsibilities carry much more weight, because he is the one that is accountable. A sister’s accountability is for herself; the husband is accountable for her, the house, the children and the nation. He is the saviour of the body. Does that not deserve honour?

When marriage is grounded in the order God established, love becomes stronger. The passion and the joy come, not romance, which is a new modern term, but the more meaningful feelings behind it, and the marriage becomes more durable over time. Marriage mirrors Christ and the Israelites, and prophecy is not entertainment: it is a sign for us to correct ourselves and get things in order, individually and as a people.

precepts.text: The order is God, Christ, man, woman. There is a leadership structure and a rank in the home before there is ever one in the church.
precepts.point: Ruling well is character, not force. Screaming and cursing is the lowest form of what you think authority is, and a tyrant at home is a spirit breaker in the congregation.

precepts.text: The flock of my pasture are men. It was men doing the sacrifice and lighting the incense and doing the service of God in the temple, never women. The service a woman does is to the man, and the man serves God. It is our job to present you holy before our Lord.
precepts.point: You will not hear of any of the hundred and forty-four thousand that were sealed being women. The woman serves the man, the man serves God, and when her man is godly they serve God together.

note.label: The 5 Signs of a Good Wife

precepts.text: Every man praying or prophesying having his head covered dishonoureth his head; the priesthood that wore the mitre has changed.
precepts.point: No man today needs to walk around in a mitre bearing iniquity and claiming a high priest's office. Christ bore our iniquities and did that work; the priesthood has changed, which is why Paul wrote what he wrote in 1 Corinthians 11. Wearing it on your own time as heritage is one thing, but when you are dealing with the scriptures, teaching, reading, studying, or praying, take it off; that is not your office.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
The plate of pure gold, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, was always upon Aaron's forehead “that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts”, that they may be accepted before the Lord. That was the high priest's office.

No man today needs to walk around in a mitre bearing iniquity and claiming a high priest's office. Christ bore our iniquities and did that work; the priesthood has changed, which is why Paul wrote: “Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonoureth his head.”

Wearing it on your own time as heritage is one thing. But when you are dealing with the scriptures, teaching, reading, studying or praying, take it off. That is not your office.

precepts.text: Take, eat, this is my body; this cup is the new testament in my blood, this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me. The cup of the covenant is why the Nazarite vow cannot be kept under Christ.
precepts.point: After that the Nazarite may drink wine; before that he could not. In our understanding today you cannot keep the vow of a Nazarite under Christ: you can let your hair grow as long as you want, but when we break bread and take the cup in remembrance of Christ, renewing that covenant, you have to drink that wine to be in covenant with him.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
When the days of his separation were fulfilled, the Nazarite offered a he lamb and a ewe lamb “without blemish”, the same thing going into Christ, with unleavened bread and the meat and drink offerings; he shaved the head of his separation and put the hair in the fire under the peace offerings, and the priest waved the sodden shoulder and the cakes before the Lord. Then “after that the Nazarite may drink wine”; before that he could not.

In our understanding today you cannot keep the vow of a Nazarite under Christ. Paul delivered what he received: “That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me. After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.”

You can let your hair grow as long as you want, but when we break bread and take the cup in remembrance of Christ, renewing that covenant, you have to drink that wine to be in covenant with him. The cup of the covenant is why the Nazarite vow cannot be kept under Christ.

precepts.text: The divine order the Most High established: the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man.
precepts.point: Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
The way back from the sodomite and the whore among our people is by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Paul gives that order: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.”

God, then Christ, then the man, then the woman. That order is the answer to the push for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians: the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and families with a father and a mother in their place.

precepts.text: The head of every man is Christ, and the head of Christ is God.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Paul lays out the order David saw: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” The head of Christ is God. That is why David could say the Lord is my rock and then the God of my rock, and the Lord said unto my Lord.

So the Rock that begat thee is Christ, the spiritual Rock that followed Israel in the wilderness, and over that Rock is his head, the Father. Of the Rock we have been unmindful, and God that formed us we have forgotten.

precepts.text: He that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself; for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. That covenant is not to be forced on children who do not yet know the Lord.
precepts.point: Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.”

That covenant is not to be forced on children who do not yet know the Lord. Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it. Samuel himself, in the house of the Lord from a child, “did not yet know the Lord.” Let them see you take that covenant until they are ready.

precepts.text: Because of disobedience many are weak and sickly, and many sleep, showing that sickness follows coming out from under the commandments.
precepts.point: His own body would be struck: he would have great sickness by disease of his bowels, until his bowels fell out by reason of the sickness day by day. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

precepts.why:
“For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep.”

Because of disobedience many are weak and sickly, and many sleep. Sickness follows coming out from under the commandments. Jehoram had not walked “in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah”, and the word to him was “great sickness by disease of thy bowels.”

precepts.text: There must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.
precepts.point: What is in a man that will not let him go on has to be cut off. Better to enter into life maimed than to keep the thing and be cast into the fire.

note.label: Matthew 18: Offences, the Rule for a Trespassing Brother, and Forgiveness

precepts.why:
“Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” Offences must come. They will come in the congregation, because everyone comes out of a different life and is still learning the others. Much of what offends is small and passes once brethren know each other.

Paul says the same of the congregation: “For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” There must be heresies, as there must be offences, and there is a purpose in it: they make manifest who is approved. The offences that come show who will go on and who will be turned aside by them.

That is why what is in a man that will not let him go on has to be cut off. If the hand, the foot or the eye offends, cut it off and cast it from you; it is better to enter into life halt or maimed than to keep the thing and be cast into everlasting fire.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 18: Babylon Is Fallen

precepts.why: Paul confirms it: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” Man was made from the dust of the ground, and the woman comes from man.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
This is another verse that trips brothers up; some of you just skip it. “For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.” Who has a number next to the word power in their Bible? It says that is a covering, in sign that she is under the power of her husband. So that is what it means by power: the power to cover her head, in obedience.
